t: The name Shiraz appears on Elamite tablets dated to 2000 BCE, but the city was founded or restored in 693 by the Umayyads and stayed a provincial town until it became the capital of the Saffarids in the late 9th century.
Under the Buyids, who made it their capital, Shiraz became the largest city of Fars, and in the 13th century it became a leading centre of the arts and letters, the home of Saadi and Hafez.

Spared by the Mongols and by Tamerlane, Shiraz was sacked after a revolt against Nader Shah, rose again as the capital of Karim Khan Zand from 1762, and was lowered to a provincial capital under the Qajars.
dyk: Shiraz was spared by both Genghis Khan and Tamerlane: its local ruler offered tribute and submission to the first, and in 1382 Shah Shoja agreed to submit to the second.
ev: Elamite clay tablets name a city called Tiraziš, the earliest reference to Shiraz
Shiraz is founded or restored by an Umayyad governor
Amr, a Saffarid ruler, founds the city's first congregational mosque
The Buyids oust the Saffarids, and Adud al-Dawla later rules from Shiraz
Forces of Ismail I, founder of the Safavid dynasty, capture the city
Karim Khan Zand makes Shiraz his capital
The Báb first declares his mission in Shiraz
A pogrom in the Jewish quarter kills 12 Jews

f.founded: Shiraz was founded or restored in 693 by Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi, brother of the Umayyad viceroy al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, or by the latter's kinsman Muhammad ibn Qasim; Elamite tablets of 2000 BCE name an earlier city called Tiraziš.
f.where: On a plain at the foot of the Zagros Mountains, 1,500 metres above sea level, in the north-west of Fars province in south-western Iran, with a seasonal river, the Dry River, flowing through its northern part.
f.known: The Elamite name Tiraziš; capital of the Saffarids and of the Buyids; Adud al-Dawla's library and hospital; the poets Saadi and Hafez; the philosopher Mulla Sadra; Karim Khan Zand's capital; the city where the Báb declared his mission in 1844
f.today: Shiraz is the capital of Fars province and the fifth most populous city of Iran.
